pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.12 a.1
pairs.question: Utrum aliquis intellectus creatus possit Deum videre per essentiam?
pairs.answer: Unde simpliciter concedendum est quod beati Dei essentiam videant.
pairs.derivation: The author poses the question (a.1 title / preamble 'utrum aliquis intellectus creatus possit videre essentiam Dei') and answers it himself. The Respondeo opens with a long non-answering preamble (the sol-and-bat analogy, then 'quidam posuerunt quod nullus intellectus creatus essentiam Dei videre potest. Sed hoc inconvenienter dicitur...') which I skip as it sets up and rejects the opposing view rather than stating Aquinas's own answer. I advance the answer-start to the concluding operative sentence 'Unde simpliciter concedendum est...' (verbatim; source has 'concedentum', a printing slip, but the answer span chosen ends the corpus reply). The terminal period is kept. Question normalized: capitalized initial, added '?'.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.12 a.4
pairs.question: Utrum aliquis intellectus creatus per sua naturalia divinam essentiam videre possit?
pairs.answer: Impossibile est quod aliquis intellectus creatus per sua naturalia essentiam Dei videat.
pairs.derivation: Author poses the question (a.4 title / preamble 'utrum aliqua substantia intellectualis creata ex suis naturalibus sufficiens sit videre Dei essentiam') and answers it in the Respondeo. Dropped the framing 'Respondeo dicendum quod'; the operative answering clause is the first sentence and is taken to its first full stop, ending before 'Cognitio enim contingit...' which begins the supporting argument. Capitalized initial 'Impossibile', kept terminal period, added '?' to question.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.12 a.7
pairs.question: Utrum videntes Deum per essentiam ipsum comprehendant?
pairs.answer: Comprehendere Deum impossibile est cuicumque intellectui creato.
pairs.derivation: Author poses the question (a.7 title / preamble 'utrum aliquis intellectus creatus possit comprehendere Dei essentiam') and answers it. Dropped framing 'Respondeo dicendum quod'. The reply's first sentence continues '...attingere vero mente Deum qualitercumque, magna est beatitudo, ut dicit Augustinus' which is a separate qualifying clause (introduced by 'vero', citing Augustine), not part of the direct answer, so I end the window at the first full stop after 'creato'. Capitalized 'Comprehendere', kept period, added '?'.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.12 a.11
pairs.question: Utrum aliquis in hac vita possit videre Deum per essentiam?
pairs.answer: Ab homine puro Deus videri per essentiam non potest, nisi ab hac vita mortali separetur.
pairs.derivation: Author poses the question (a.11 title / preamble 'utrum in statu huius vitae possit aliquis homo essentiam Dei videre') and answers it. Dropped framing 'Respondeo dicendum quod'. Answer is the first sentence to its full stop; what follows ('Cuius ratio est quia...') is the justification and is cut. Capitalized 'Ab', kept period, added '?'.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.12 a.13
pairs.question: Utrum per gratiam habeatur altior cognitio Dei quam ea quae habetur per rationem naturalem?
pairs.answer: Per gratiam perfectior cognitio de Deo habetur a nobis, quam per rationem naturalem.
pairs.derivation: Author poses the question (a.13 title / preamble 'utrum, supra cognitionem naturalis rationis, sit in praesenti vita aliqua cognitio Dei per gratiam') and answers it. Dropped framing 'Respondeo dicendum quod'. Answer is the first sentence to its full stop; what follows ('Quod sic patet...') begins the demonstration and is cut. Capitalized 'Per', kept period, added '?'.
